fix: Replace the `object[]` fallback with `never`: `Promise<InstanceType<This> extends BasePlacement<any, infer D> ? D[] : never>`
note: Because `This extends typeof BasePlacement`, `InstanceType<This>` always extends `BasePlacement<any, any>`, so the conditional's false branch (`object[]`) is structurally unreachable. Using `never` makes the dead branch explicit and avoids implying that the method could legitimately return `object[]`. The fix is a minor cleanup — it does not affect real-world call sites — so severity is low rather than medium.

While the runtime JSDoc loosely annotates it as {object} and the body ignores the parameter in favour of this.document.actor.system.attributes.hp, the declared interface should match the actual call site type for type safety on any override. Genuine fidelity gap, but low severity since the parameter is effectively unused.

fix: Export `interface Registry` so consumers can do `import type { Registry } from '.../registry.d.mts'` and re-open it via module augmentation, or move it into a `declare global { namespace dnd5e { interface Registry { ... } } }` block so it participates in the open `dnd5e` namespace that modules can already augment.
note: Confirmed real but low impact. The `Registry` interface is module-private (not exported), so third-party modules have no way to declaration-merge additional registry entries (e.g. `monsters: ItemRegistry`). Since `dnd5e.registry` is typed as `typeof import('./registry.mjs').default` which resolves to `Registry`, any augmentation path requires the interface to be accessible. The finding is genuine, though many consumers may simply cast or use `as` instead.
